court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: Indian country status
issues.why: Federal jurisdiction and MCA/GCA/ACA applicability depend on whether the conduct occurred in Indian country.

issues.label: Defendant Indian status
issues.why: Mr. Smith’s Indian status triggers MCA analysis and affects GCA exclusions.

issues.label: Victim Indian status
issues.why: Victim’s Indian status affects GCA applicability and the jurisdictional framework for non-Indian defendants.

issues.label: Proper charging statute use
issues.why: Court must confirm MCA properly charges Mr. Smith and ACA-as-applied-through-GCA properly charges Mrs. Smith.

issues.label: Castro-Huerta jurisdiction claim
issues.why: Court must decide whether state concurrent jurisdiction over non-Indian defendants affects or negates federal jurisdiction here.

issues.label: Federal subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm the district court had jurisdiction under 18 U.S.C. § 3231 and the substantive jurisdictional statutes.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction over defendants
issues.why: Court must ensure defendants were properly before the federal court (rarely disputed but required).

issues.label: MCA offense coverage
issues.why: Court must confirm Oklahoma child abuse/neglect are properly assimilated/incorporated as MCA offenses for an Indian defendant.

issues.label: ACA applicability in Indian country
issues.why: Court must confirm ACA can supply the substantive offense for a non-Indian in Indian country via the GCA.

issues.label: GCA exclusions effect
issues.why: Court must decide how §1152 exclusions (Indian-on-Indian; Indian already punished; treaty) interact with aiding/abetting theories.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting legal theory
issues.why: Court must determine whether 18 U.S.C. § 2 permits convicting each defendant as an aider/abettor given MCA/GCA/ACA limits.

issues.label: Non-Indian aiding MCA charge
issues.why: Court must decide if a non-Indian may be convicted as an aider/abettor to an MCA offense charged against an Indian principal.

issues.label: Indian aiding GCA/ACA charge
issues.why: Court must decide if an Indian may be convicted as an aider/abettor to a GCA/ACA offense given §1152’s Indian-on-Indian exclusion.

issues.label: Instruction preservation/waiver
issues.why: Court must decide whether the aiding-and-abetting objection was timely and properly preserved for appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review instruction
issues.why: If not preserved, the court must apply plain-error review rather than de novo/abuse-of-discretion.

issues.label: Instruction correctness
issues.why: Court must determine whether the aiding-and-abetting instruction accurately stated the law and fit the evidence.

issues.label: Constructive amendment/variance
issues.why: Court must assess whether aiding-and-abetting instructions or proofs altered the indictment’s charges or created a prejudicial variance.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence counts
issues.why: Court must ensure evidence supports each element of child abuse and child neglect (and aiding/abetting if relied on).

issues.label: Elements of OK §843.5(A)
issues.why: Court must identify and apply the precise elements and mens rea for Oklahoma child abuse by injury.

issues.label: Elements of OK §843.5(C)
issues.why: Court must identify and apply the precise elements and mens rea for Oklahoma child neglect.

issues.label: Assimilation prerequisites
issues.why: For ACA counts, court must confirm no federal statute already punishes the same conduct, and assimilation is proper.

issues.label: Double jeopardy/merger concerns
issues.why: Court must consider whether abuse and neglect counts punish the same conduct or require distinct elements under Blockburger/merger principles.

issues.label: Multiplicity of counts
issues.why: Court must ensure indictment does not charge the same offense in multiple counts leading to multiple punishments.

issues.label: Jury unanimity issues
issues.why: Court must consider whether the instructions required unanimity as to specific acts supporting abuse/neglect.

issues.label: Evidentiary fairness at trial
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether any evidentiary rulings (including identity references to H.M./M.V./K.B.) caused prejudice affecting verdict.

issues.label: Bruton/Confrontation in joint trial
issues.why: Court must ensure joint trial and any statements did not violate confrontation rights or require severance.

issues.label: Severance considerations
issues.why: Court must consider whether joint trial with divergent defenses created compelling prejudice under Rule 14.

issues.label: Rule 29 motion standards
issues.why: Court must apply the correct sufficiency standard for judgment of acquittal and the timing/renewal requirements.

issues.label: Rule 33 motion standards
issues.why: Court must apply the correct “interest of justice” standard, including timeliness and newly-discovered-evidence rules.

issues.label: Timeliness of second motions
issues.why: Court must decide whether Mrs. Smith’s post-sentencing amended Rule 29/33 motion was jurisdictionally/time barred.

issues.label: Excusable neglect extension
issues.why: Court must consider whether Rule 45 permits an extension for late Rule 33 filing and whether the court had authority to grant it.

issues.label: Jurisdiction vs claim-processing
issues.why: Court must classify the Rule 33 time limit as jurisdictional or a claim-processing rule affecting enforcement.

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and finality
issues.why: Court must ensure notices/timelines support appellate jurisdiction over convictions and sentences.

issues.label: Guideline selection step
issues.why: Court must start with U.S.S.G. §1B1.2 to identify an applicable guideline or proceed under §2X5.1.

issues.label: Analogous guideline required
issues.why: Court must decide whether a “sufficiently analogous” guideline exists for OK child abuse/neglect and apply it if so.

issues.label: Aggravated assault analogy
issues.why: Court must decide whether U.S.S.G. §2A2.2 is the most analogous guideline for child abuse by injury on these facts.

issues.label: Alternative analogous guidelines
issues.why: Court must consider other potential analogs (e.g., assault/abuse guidelines) before defaulting to no-guideline treatment.

issues.label: Error in PSR guideline view
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSR’s “no guideline so §3553 controls” misapplied §2X5.1 and affected procedure.

issues.label: Procedural reasonableness
issues.why: Court must decide whether the sentencing court correctly calculated the Guidelines and explained the chosen sentence.

issues.label: Harmlessness of guideline error
issues.why: If guideline miscalculation occurred, court must decide whether the error was harmless under governing standards.

issues.label: Statutory maximums per count
issues.why: Court must confirm maximum penalties under assimilated Oklahoma law and federal charging statutes, including any life-maximum claim.

issues.label: Consecutive/concurrent authority
issues.why: Court must ensure concurrency decisions complied with statute and Guidelines framework.

issues.label: Substantive reasonableness
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether 180/240 months are substantively reasonable under §3553(a) given facts and disparities.

issues.label: Due process at sentencing
issues.why: Court must ensure defendants had notice and opportunity to rebut sentencing information used by the court.

issues.label: Victim-impact letters timing
issues.why: Court must decide whether refusing continuance to review late letters violated Rule 32, due process, or §3553 procedures.

issues.label: Crime Victims’ Rights Act scope
issues.why: Court must determine whether letter-writers qualify as “victims” under 18 U.S.C. §3771(e)(2).

issues.label: Non-victim statements use
issues.why: Court must decide whether the court may consider statements from non-victims and under what limits/relevance.

issues.label: Disclosure obligations Rule 32
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the government/court complied with Rule 32 disclosure requirements for sentencing materials.

issues.label: Reliability of sentencing info
issues.why: Court must ensure any victim-impact information considered had sufficient indicia of reliability.

issues.label: Remedy for letter error
issues.why: If error occurred, court must decide whether resentencing is required and before whom (same or different judge).

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting verdict basis
issues.why: Court must consider whether the jury could have convicted on an invalid aiding/abetting theory requiring reversal under alternative-theory doctrine.

issues.label: Instruction error prejudice
issues.why: Court must assess whether any aiding-and-abetting instruction error affected substantial rights or verdict outcome.

issues.label: Sufficiency as principal vs aider
issues.why: Court must determine whether evidence supports conviction as a principal even if aiding/abetting theory fails.

issues.label: Mens rea for aiding/abetting
issues.why: Court must ensure instruction required intent to facilitate and knowledge of the crime, not mere presence or association.

issues.label: Treaty exception under §1152
issues.why: Court must consider whether any treaty provisions remove federal jurisdiction (often overlooked, but part of §1152).

issues.label: State vs federal concurrent power
issues.why: Court must reconcile federal prosecution with any concurrent state authority recognized in Castro-Huerta without preemption issues.

issues.label: Assimilated-law elements proof
issues.why: Court must ensure the jury was correctly instructed on, and evidence proved, all incorporated Oklahoma-law elements.

issues.label: Sentencing disparities consideration
issues.why: Court must consider §3553(a)(6) unwarranted disparity, including between co-defendants and similar federal cases.

issues.label: Preservation of sentencing issues
issues.why: Court must decide whether objections to guideline choice and victim letters were preserved and set the standard of review.
